Raise to Speak listing copy vs Siri engineering — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate system AirPods Siri gestures with storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Raise to Speak on the device — when enabled on supported AirPods, lifting the earbuds toward your mouth activates Siri so you can speak a request without saying "Hey Siri". Toggle under Settings → Siri & Search → Raise to Speak (抬起讲话). Some models also market Ultra Raise to Speak for extended gesture sensitivity. System AirPods behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • SiriKit, App Intents, and in-app voice UX — custom Siri shortcuts, INIntent handlers, voice-triggered app flows, and microphone routing inside your binary. Engineering inside the app — not listing rewrite.
  • Raise to Speak marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app pairs well with Raise to Speak, supports hands-free Siri via AirPods lift-to-talk, or shows gallery frames of "Talk to Siri without Hey Siri" workflows. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Raise to Speak.

An app that references Raise to Speak in onboarding and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe lift-AirPods-to-talk-to-Siri workflows on the store page, not whether Raise to Speak toggles inside iOS Settings.

Raise to Speak-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

AirPods Siri gesture marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general Siri guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Raise to Speak in iOS Settings — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Raise to Speak vs Raise to Wake — do not conflate

US pages sometimes mention both "raise" gestures on the same AirPods or iPhone gallery. China storefront copy must keep them distinct: 抬起讲话 / 抬起耳机讲话 for AirPods Raise to Speak under Siri & Search; 抬起唤醒 / 拿起唤醒 for iPhone display wake under Display & Brightness → Raise to Wake. Raise to Speak activates Siri when you lift AirPods toward your mouth; Raise to Wake turns on the iPhone lock screen when you pick up the phone. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope — if your English source only markets Raise to Speak, we do not upgrade to Raise to Wake 抬起唤醒 claims in subtitle, keywords, or overlays. See our Raise to Wake listing guide only if display wake is your lead claim.

Official Settings vocabulary

Apple's zh-Hans Settings UI uses 抬起讲话 for Raise to Speak, with related buyer language around 抬起耳机讲话 (lift AirPods to speak), 抬起耳机对 Siri 说话 (lift AirPods to talk to Siri), and 无需说嘿 Siri (without saying Hey Siri). Listing copy should mirror that vocabulary — not generic 语音助手 or 嘿 Siri that could mean always-listen Hey Siri marketing, Type to Siri keyboard input, or App Intents spoken shortcuts.

Ultra Raise to Speak

Some AirPods models market extended gesture sensitivity as Ultra Raise to Speak. zh-Hans listing copy should describe the buyer benefit — faster hands-free Siri activation, lift-to-talk without voice trigger — without inventing hardware claims your English source does not make. AppLocale keeps Ultra Raise to Speak phrasing aligned with your US gallery scope.

Raise to Speak vs Type to Siri

Type to Siri sends typed text into Siri as a request — 键入 Siri — under Accessibility settings. Raise to Speak sends spoken requests via an AirPods lift gesture. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 键入 Siri when your English source only shows a Raise to Speak toggle. See the Type to Siri listing guide only if silent keyboard Siri input is your lead marketing claim.

Raise to Speak vs Announce Notifications and Announce Calls

Announce Notifications speaks notification content aloud — 朗读通知. Announce Calls speaks caller information — 来电播报. Raise to Speak lets the user initiate Siri by lifting AirPods. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 朗读通知 or 来电播报 when your English source only shows Raise to Speak Siri input. See the Announce Notifications listing guide or Announce Calls listing guide only if spoken notification or call output is your lead claim.

Raise to Speak vs Conversation Boost, Transparency, and Headphone Accommodations

Conversation Boost amplifies voices in Transparency mode — often marketed under Headphone Accommodations as 透明模式对话增强. Transparency mode (通透模式) passes ambient sound. Headphone Accommodations tunes EQ and soft-sound amplification — 耳机调节. Raise to Speak is a Siri input gesture, not an audio tuning or listening-mode feature. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 通透模式 or 耳机调节 when your English source only shows Raise to Speak. See the Headphone Accommodations listing guide or Noise Cancellation listing guide only if those are your lead marketing claims.

AppLocale FAQ

Is Raise to Speak the same as Raise to Wake on the listing?

No. Raise to Speak markets lifting AirPods toward your mouth to activate Siri without Hey Siri — 抬起讲话, 抬起耳机讲话. Raise to Wake markets lifting iPhone to wake the lock screen display — 抬起唤醒, 拿起唤醒. One is AirPods Siri input; the other is iPhone display wake. See our Raise to Wake listing guide for display wake copy.

Is Raise to Speak the same as Type to Siri?

No. Raise to Speak is spoken Siri input via an AirPods lift gesture. Type to Siri is keyboard text input under Accessibility → Siri → Type to Siri — 键入 Siri. See our Type to Siri listing guide for silent keyboard Siri copy.

Is Raise to Speak the same as Announce Notifications or Announce Calls?

No. Raise to Speak lets users initiate Siri by lifting AirPods. Announce Notifications speaks notification content aloud — 朗读通知. Announce Calls speaks caller information — 来电播报. See our Announce Notifications listing guide or Announce Calls listing guide for spoken output copy.

Is Raise to Speak the same as Conversation Boost or Transparency mode?

No. Raise to Speak is a Siri activation gesture. Conversation Boost amplifies voices in Transparency mode — often under Headphone Accommodations as 透明模式对话增强. Transparency mode (通透模式) is an AirPods listening mode. See our Headphone Accommodations listing guide or Noise Cancellation listing guide for audio tuning and listening-mode copy.
